events.title: HODL is born

research.summary: BitcoinTalk user GameKyuubi titled a post 'I AM HODLING,' a drunken misspelling of holding that immediately became community slang.
research.significance: HODL became one of crypto's most durable memes and a shorthand for refusing to sell through volatility.

events.title: Dogecoin launches

research.summary: Dogecoin launched on 6 December 2013, created by Billy Markus and Jackson Palmer around the Doge meme.
research.significance: Dogecoin fused cryptocurrency with internet meme culture and pioneered tipping, community fundraising and later meme-coin culture.

events.title: Ethereum whitepaper

research.summary: Ethereum's official history dates the introductory whitepaper to 27 November 2013; Vitalik Buterin had circulated the first draft to prospective collaborators that month.
research.significance: The paper proposed a general-purpose blockchain for smart contracts and decentralized applications, expanding the idea of blockchain beyond money.

events.title: Cyprus banking crisis draws attention to Bitcoin

research.summary: Bitcoin rose sharply during the Cyprus banking crisis, while contemporary reporting linked part of the interest to concern over deposit losses and capital controls.
research.significance: The episode helped establish Bitcoin's 'outside the banking system' and safe-haven narrative, but the crisis should not be treated as the sole proven cause of the rally.

sources.title: CNN Money — Bitcoin prices surge post-Cyprus bailout

research.notes: Causal wording kept cautious: contemporary correlation/narrative, not proof that Cypriot depositors drove the move.

events.title: Bitcoin first trades above $100

research.summary: Bitcoin traded above $100 for the first time on 1 April 2013 on Mt. Gox-era markets.
research.significance: Crossing three figures marked Bitcoin's transition from niche experiment to an asset attracting broad speculative attention.

events.title: Silk Road is shut down and Ross Ulbricht arrested

research.summary: Federal agents arrested Ross Ulbricht in a San Francisco library and seized his laptop; the Silk Road site was shut down in the same enforcement operation.
research.significance: The takedown was a landmark test of Bitcoin-linked law enforcement, darknet-market investigation and blockchain evidence.

sources.title: FBI — Ross Ulbricht laptop / Silk Road history

events.title: Bitcoin first trades above $1,000

research.summary: Bitcoin traded above $1,000 for the first time on Mt. Gox on 27 November 2013.
research.significance: The milestone capped Bitcoin's first truly global speculative boom and made a four-digit BTC price a mainstream financial story.

events.title: China begins major restrictions on Bitcoin financial services

research.summary: Chinese authorities stated that Bitcoin was a virtual commodity rather than legal currency and barred financial and payment institutions from Bitcoin-related business.
research.significance: This was the first major national-level regulatory shock from China and began a recurring China-policy theme in crypto markets.

sources.title: People's Daily / PBOC — Bitcoin notice Q&A

events.title: US FinCEN issues landmark virtual-currency guidance

research.summary: FinCEN issued interpretive guidance distinguishing virtual-currency users from administrators and exchangers and applying money-transmitter rules to qualifying businesses.
research.significance: It was a foundational US federal regulatory framework for cryptocurrency businesses.

events.title: First publicly accessible Bitcoin ATM launches in Vancouver

research.summary: A Robocoin kiosk at Waves Coffee House in Vancouver went live as the world's first publicly accessible two-way Bitcoin ATM.
research.significance: The machine made exchanging cash and bitcoin a physical, walk-up consumer experience.

sources.title: CityNews Vancouver — world's first Bitcoin ATM

events.title: James Howells' lost-hard-drive Bitcoin story gains public attention

research.summary: James Howells' story became public when UK media reported that a hard drive containing keys to roughly 7,500 BTC had been discarded and buried in a Newport landfill.
research.significance: It became crypto's archetypal lost-keys story and a vivid lesson in self-custody irreversibility.

sources.title: The Guardian — missing hard drive in Newport landfill

events.title: Mastercoin conducts an early token sale on Bitcoin

research.summary: J.R. Willett's Mastercoin project used a Bitcoin 'Exodus Address' fundraiser: contributors sent BTC during August and received protocol-layer Mastercoins.
research.significance: This is one of the clearest ancestors of the ICO/token-sale model and an early attempt to build programmable assets on Bitcoin.

sources.title: Omni Foundation — Brief History of Mastercoin

events.title: Cyprus capital controls fuel Bitcoin safe-haven narratives

research.summary: This is the same Cyprus/Bitcoin safe-haven narrative captured in LORE-EVT-0081.
research.significance: Keep as contextual framing, not a separate card event.

sources.title: CNN Money — Bitcoin prices surge post-Cyprus bailout

events.title: US Senate hearings give Bitcoin unexpected legitimacy

research.summary: The US Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee held its first congressional hearing focused on virtual currencies, hearing from regulators, law enforcement and industry participants.
research.significance: The hearing marked a shift from treating Bitcoin mainly as a criminal curiosity toward formal consideration of both risks and legitimate uses.

sources.title: US Senate HSGAC — Beyond Silk Road hearing

events.title: Silk Road seizure proves Bitcoin transactions can become legal evidence

research.summary: Federal authorities seized Silk Road infrastructure and tens of thousands of BTC, later identifying additional wallets on Ulbricht's computer.
research.significance: The seizure demonstrated that pseudonymous blockchain assets could be traced, confiscated and treated as forfeitable property.

events.title: Ross Ulbricht is arrested in a San Francisco library

research.summary: Ulbricht was arrested while using his laptop in a San Francisco library, allowing agents to seize the running computer.
research.significance: The arrest method became a defining human-detail in the Silk Road story.

sources.title: FBI — Ross Ulbricht laptop / Silk Road history

events.title: Bitcoin China becomes one of the world's largest exchanges

research.summary: BTC China was reported as the world's largest Bitcoin exchange by trading volume in November 2013 during a surge in Chinese participation.
research.significance: China became a central force in Bitcoin trading, foreshadowing years of market sensitivity to Chinese policy.

sources.title: TechCrunch — BTC China largest by volume

events.title: People's Bank of China bars financial institutions from Bitcoin business

research.summary: This describes the same PBOC-led restriction on financial institutions as LORE-EVT-0085.
research.significance: Canonicalized to LORE-EVT-0085.

sources.title: People's Daily / PBOC — Bitcoin notice Q&A

events.title: Mastercoin becomes one of the first major token-layer projects on Bitcoin

research.summary: Mastercoin became an early token-layer protocol on Bitcoin and distributed its native asset via the Exodus fundraiser.
research.significance: Technical significance of the canonical Mastercoin token-sale event.

sources.title: Omni Foundation — Brief History of Mastercoin

events.title: Avalon ships early commercial Bitcoin ASIC miners

research.summary: Avalon's team announced that its first ASIC batch had shipped on 20 January 2013, not in 2012.
research.significance: The shipment marks the arrival of commercially delivered ASIC hardware and a decisive new era in Bitcoin mining.

events.title: BitInstant raises $1.5m led by Winklevoss Capital

research.summary: By May 2013, Charlie Shrem was CEO of BitInstant, vice chairman of the Bitcoin Foundation and a highly visible speaker in the early Bitcoin startup scene. BitInstant was reported to be processing roughly 30% of money moving into and out of Bitcoin.
research.significance: Shrem became one of the first recognizable Bitcoin entrepreneurs, making his later arrest and conviction especially significant to the industry's early regulatory history.

sources.title: US DOJ — Charlie Shrem case background

research.notes: Vague prominence row narrowed to a specific financing milestone.

events.title: Coinbase raises prominent venture backing

research.summary: Coinbase raised major venture funding as it scaled its consumer Bitcoin wallet and on-ramp.
research.significance: The funding helped signal venture capital's growing confidence in crypto infrastructure, but a specific round should replace this broad row if retained.
research.notes: Needs round-specific primary/SEC/VC source before canonical publication.

events.title: Kraken launches after years of post-Mt Gox development

research.summary: Kraken opened for trading with euro, bitcoin and litecoin markets on 10 September 2013.
research.significance: Kraken became one of the longest-lived major centralized exchanges and emphasized compliance/security from launch.

events.title: LocalBitcoins expands peer-to-peer Bitcoin trading worldwide

research.summary: LocalBitcoins had expanded into a global peer-to-peer marketplace by mid-2013. Retrospective platform data reports about 44,000 users across 142 countries by its first anniversary, while contemporary WIRED reporting described it as ground zero for face-to-face Bitcoin trading.
research.significance: LocalBitcoins became crucial infrastructure for buying Bitcoin with local cash and bank methods where conventional exchanges were unavailable or intrusive.

sources.title: WIRED — Why the Only Real Way to Buy Bitcoins Is on the Streets
Odaily retrospective — LocalBitcoins first-anniversary user/country figures

research.notes: Use platform-scale figures as retrospective data; WIRED provides contemporary evidence of its importance.

events.title: Bitcoin Foundation faces internal controversies

research.summary: The Bitcoin Foundation faced governance and personality controversies during the early Bitcoin era.
research.significance: Too broad for a canonical event; requires a named resignation, scandal, election or policy dispute.

events.title: US Treasury FinCEN guidance distinguishes users, exchangers and administrators

research.summary: This is the same FinCEN guidance and its user/exchanger/administrator distinction.
research.significance: Canonicalized to LORE-EVT-0144.

events.title: BaFin recognizes Bitcoin as a unit of account in Germany

research.summary: Germany's finance ministry recognized Bitcoin as a 'unit of account' for regulatory/tax purposes, while not treating it as legal tender.
research.significance: One of the earliest significant formal classifications of Bitcoin by a major European government.

sources.title: The Guardian — Germany recognizes Bitcoin as unit of account

events.title: Thailand Bitcoin-ban headlines spark debate over what constitutes a ban

research.summary: Bitcoin Co. Ltd. said it suspended operations after Bank of Thailand officials advised that multiple Bitcoin activities were illegal because no applicable legal framework existed. Contemporary reporting called this a 'ban,' but the episode did not amount to a clearly documented nationwide statutory prohibition.
research.significance: The incident is an early example of crypto headlines outrunning legal precision and helped establish the recurring 'country bans Bitcoin' news cycle.
research.notes: Keep wording explicitly qualified as a reported regulator position, not an enacted blanket statute.

events.title: Baidu briefly accepts Bitcoin for selected services

research.summary: Baidu's Jiasule web-security service began accepting Bitcoin payments, announced publicly on 15 October.
research.significance: A major Chinese internet brand briefly accepting Bitcoin became a striking adoption signal immediately before China's December restriction.

sources.title: Baidu Jiasule announcement archived via BitcoinTalk

events.title: Bitcoiners use Casascius coins as physical bearer collectibles

research.summary: Casascius coins became prized physical bearer collectibles as early Bitcoin adoption grew.
research.significance: This is cultural context flowing from the canonical 2011 Casascius launch rather than a separate 2013 event.

events.title: James Howells begins efforts to recover discarded Bitcoin hard drive

research.summary: Howells began seeking recovery of the discarded hard drive as the value of the lost BTC became widely publicized.
research.significance: The recovery campaign belongs under the canonical 2013 lost-hard-drive story unless later legal milestones are treated separately.

sources.title: The Guardian — missing hard drive in Newport landfill

events.title: BTC Guild grows into a dominant Bitcoin mining pool

research.summary: Academic measurements of Bitcoin mining in spring/summer 2013 showed BTC Guild and 50BTC together controlling more than 55% of network hashing power for part of the period.
research.significance: The concentration made BTC Guild a central case in early debate over whether pooled mining could undermine Bitcoin's decentralization.

sources.title: IACR ePrint — Is Bitcoin a Decentralized Currency?

events.title: ASIC resistance becomes a design goal for several altcoins

research.summary: As Bitcoin mining became dominated by specialized ASICs, alternative cryptocurrencies increasingly experimented with memory-hard algorithms such as Scrypt and later explicit ASIC-resistance strategies.
research.significance: ASIC resistance became a recurring design and governance question: whether mining should remain accessible to commodity hardware or optimize for specialized efficiency.

sources.title: IACR ePrint — Bitcoin mining concentration in 2013

research.notes: Trend/context row; explicit anti-ASIC projects such as Vertcoin are cleaner later milestones.

events.title: Reddit Bitcoin tipping grows rapidly

research.summary: Reddit's /u/bitcointip bot let users tip Bitcoin through comments and private messages; by 2013 tipping strangers had become a recognizable part of early Bitcoin internet culture.
research.significance: Tiny tips exposed people to Bitcoin without an exchange account and helped frame BTC as native internet money rather than only an investment.
research.notes: The bot existed in 2012; 2013 represents cultural growth, not launch.

events.title: Changpeng Zhao enters Bitcoin industry after poker-game introduction lore

research.summary: Changpeng Zhao has recounted that Bobby Lee and Ron Cao introduced him to Bitcoin during a poker game in Shanghai in 2013.
research.significance: The story became the origin lore for the future Binance founder's move into cryptocurrency.

sources.title: CNA/Bloomberg — CZ's 2013 poker-game introduction to Bitcoin

events.title: Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss disclose large Bitcoin holdings

research.summary: Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss publicly disclosed an approximately $11 million Bitcoin position; later reporting said their holdings were around 1% of circulating BTC.
research.significance: Their disclosure was an early example of prominent wealthy investors treating Bitcoin as a serious asset allocation.

events.title: Roger Ver funds early Bitcoin startups

research.summary: BitPay announced its first outside financing round in January 2013 with Roger Ver among the angel investors; Ver paid his investment contribution in Bitcoin.
research.significance: Ver's early investments in Bitcoin businesses helped fund the first generation of commercial infrastructure and reinforced his 'Bitcoin Jesus' evangelist reputation.
research.notes: Rewritten around a documented investment rather than a vague claim that he funded startups generally.

events.title: FBI seizes Silk Road servers

research.summary: This row refers to the Silk Road server/site seizure occurring with the Ulbricht arrest.
research.significance: Canonicalized to LORE-EVT-0083.

events.title: CryptoLocker ransomware popularizes Bitcoin ransom payments

research.summary: CryptoLocker emerged in 2013 as ransomware that encrypted victims' files and demanded ransom, often using Bitcoin as the payment rail.
research.significance: It helped establish the association between cryptocurrency and ransomware payments that would become a major cybercrime theme.

events.title: SEC charges Bitcoin Savings & Trust operator over Ponzi scheme

research.summary: The SEC formally charged Trendon Shavers and Bitcoin Savings & Trust with operating a Bitcoin-denominated Ponzi scheme on 23 July 2013.
research.significance: This is the enforcement milestone; it should not be dated 2012 merely because the scheme ended then.

sources.title: SEC — charges Trendon Shavers / Bitcoin Savings and Trust

events.title: Armory popularizes advanced cold-storage practices

research.summary: Bitcoin Armory made offline 'cold storage' practical through watching-only wallets and offline signing, bringing an advanced key-security model to users managing larger Bitcoin balances.
research.significance: Armory helped turn cold storage from an expert technique into recognizable wallet functionality and influenced later self-custody products.
research.notes: Context/adoption row; not asserting cold storage itself was invented in 2013.

events.title: Silk Road vendor ecosystem collapses after FBI seizure

research.summary: The original Silk Road vendor ecosystem was abruptly disrupted when authorities seized the marketplace.
research.significance: This is consequence/context of the canonical Silk Road takedown.

events.title: Silk Road 2.0 repeats darknet-market model

research.summary: Silk Road 2.0 launched in early November 2013, shortly after the original Silk Road was seized, rather than in 2014.
research.significance: Its rapid reappearance showed the resilience and replicability of darknet-market models.

sources.title: US DOJ — Operator of Silk Road 2.0 charged
